newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks extend winning streak at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks extend winning streak at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks charged higher at the close Thursday, following through on their four-day rally and drawing fresh momentum from Wall Street, dealers said.
"The market is going through a very good patch which was bolstered today by the latest U.S. data showing the economy is behaving just as everyone hoped," said Andres McKiguan at Velox traders.
Traders forecast stocks would keep a positive bias Friday.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV gained 1.4 percent to 605.24, extending its four-day advance to 4.5 percent.
The MerVal stands 6.1 percent higher so far this month.
"Local and foreign conditions are such that the MerVal should go in search of the 620 mark," setting a new high for 1996, said McKiguan.

Traders noted while the latest U.S. inflation and sales indictors matched expectations, Wall Street had not yet performed a downward correction following the re-election of President Bill Clinton November 5.
"Both their market and ours could be headed for a technical pullback, but both also have good domestic economic factors to latch on to," said a dealer at a large local brokerage.
Local sentiment has been boosted by good company results recently and by gross domestic product growth of 6.6 percent in the third quarter.
Floor volume picked up to 28.4 million pesos Thursday from 23 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 131 million pesos compared to Wednesday's hefty 159 million.
The broad market added 1.0 percent, with risers beating decliners 47 to 13 and 18 issues ending flat.
Best blue-chip performers were steelmaker Acindar, Banco de Galicia and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which surged 4.9 percent, 4.3 percent and 4.2 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by oil company Sol Petroleo, Bansud bank and steelmaker Siderca, which shed 4.0 percent, 1.1 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.
